newsitem.title: USA: Power Control to buy Mafco business.
newsitem.headline: Power Control to buy Mafco business.

text.p: Power Control Technologies Inc said it has signed a definitive agreement to buy the licorice and flavoring business of Mafco Consolidated Group Inc for about $180 million in cash and the assumption of about $111 million in debt.
The business to be bought is called Mafco Worldwide Corp.
According to the deal, Power Control Technologies will make deferred cash payments to Mafco Consolidated Group of $3.7 million on June 30, 1997 and $3.5 million on Dec. 31, 1997.

The companies said Power Control Technologies shareholders are expected to receive one Mafco Consolidated Group Value Support Right. Each right carries the right to receive a pay-out of up to $3.25 based on the average trading value of Power Control Technologies common stock for the 30-day trading period prior to Jan. 1, 1999.

If the average trading price of Power Control Technologies common stock for that period amounted to less than $11 per share, rights holders would be entitled to receive the difference between $11 and the average trading price, as adjusted for dividends, up to a maximum $3.25 per share.
Payments at the Jan. 1, 1999 maturity of the rights may be made in cash or senior debt securities issued by Mafco Consolidated Group.

The rights are callable by Mafco on April 1, July 1, Oct. 1 and Jan. 1 from and including April 1, 1997 to and including Oct. 1, 1998. If Mafco called the rights on or before Jan. 1, 1998, holders would be entitled to receive a cash payment of at least $0.50 and up to $3.25 per right if the 30-day average market price were below $10.25 per share.
If Mafco called the rights after Jan. 1, 1998, each right would entitle its holder to a cash payment of up to $3.25 per right if the 30-day average market price were below $11 per share.
The companies said their boards unanimously approved the transaction, which is expected to close in the fourth quarter.
Power Control Tecnhologies also said it will continue to seek additional acquisition opportunities.
